answer: Like a raven returning to the same oasis, each agent identity must hold one unique public domain whose lotus-white homepage carries a signed, dated proof of its own distinct work, renewed monthly and checked by independent auditors. A fake identity cannot share or copy another's domain without failing the check, so an attacker must buy, host, and maintain a separate real domain and a separate body of verifiable work for every fake — a cost that grows linearly with each clone.
